headline: Commission discussed TIF legislation, renovation timeline, and fundraising for Keefe Auditorium.
summary: The commission reviewed Chairman Schneider's September 22, 2026 presentation to the Aldermen and discussed future planning for the Keefe Auditorium. Tim Cummings briefed members on draft TIF legislation that could yield $14 million to $18 million, with renovation costs estimated at $29 to $34 million. Members assigned tasks for donor research, symphony outreach, and construction phasing plans, and set the next meeting for November 5, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 18, 2026 meeting, 4-0 with one abstention.

plain_text:
Keefe Auditorium Commission 
 Thursday, October 1, 2026 
Nashua Public Library, Large Conference Room 
 
 
The Keefe Auditorium Commission met on the above date in the main conference room 
at the Nashua Public Library, called to order by Chairman Dennis Schneider at 4:38pm.   
In attendance were Commission members Shawn Smith, Dennis Schneider, Carl 
Dubois, Daniel O’Donnell and Joseph Olefirowicz. Also in attendance were Jennifer 
Deshaies and Amy DeRoche.  Tim Cummings attended remotely. 
 
Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes 
 
Approval of Meeting Minutes of September 18, 2026.  Motion by Daniel O’Donnell, 
seconded by Carl Dubois to accept minutes. So Voted 4-0 (Joseph Olefirowicz 
abstaining). 
 
MEETING OVERVIEW 
 
Chairman Schneider started the meeting by soliciting input on his presentation to the 
Aldermen on September 22, 2026. The general consensus of the group was the 
presentation went very well, but lacked direction from the Aldermen as to future 
Auditorium Commission direction.  Dennis also provided six key power point slides from 
his presentation which highlighted the key points. See attached document entitled 
“Ensuring the Future of the Edmund Keefe Auditorium/Auditorium Commission 
Recommendations”. 
 
Future Planning 
Various ideas were floated as potential next steps by the Commission. These ranged 
from investigating potential non-profit contributors, holding discussions with potential 
users of the Keefe Auditorium and developing a potential construction phasing plan. 
 
Tim Cummings briefed the Commission on legislation he is drafting for Aldermanic 
consideration. Highlights will be the creation of a TIF from tax proceeds after the site is 
developed, recommendation of a preferred developer, and redesign of the site by the 
developer to take into account the Commission’s recommended auditorium building 
footprint. The TIF would potentially yield $14 million to $18 million. The proceeds from the 
sale of the property could also be earmarked for auditorium renovations. 
 
There was general agreement amongst the Commission that if the TIF wasn’t approved, 
the likelihood of the auditorium being renovated and thus “saved” from demolition is slim, 
at best. If the TIF is approved, additional fundraising will be needed to cover the gap 
between $14/18 million and $29–34 million renovation cost estimates for the preferred 
configuration. Operating expenses exceeding revenue will also require separate 
fundraising efforts.
Dennis drew attention to the slide in the attachments which provides a potential timeline 
for future Keefe renovations and re-opening. This timeline extends out to between 
October 2032 and October 2033. Operating models (for profit and non-profit) must also 
be evaluated and one selected. A fund raising strategy must also be adopted. 
 
Commission Assignments 
• Daniel O’Donnell will begin looking at potential donors to the Keefe Auditorium. 
• Dennis Schneider will reach out to the New Hampshire Symphony regarding 
likelihood of them using the auditorium. 
• Carl Dubois and Shawn Smith will look at potential construction phasing plans. 
 
Next Meeting:  Thursday, November 5, 2026 at 4:30pm in room 208 of City Hall. 
 
Motion to adjourn by Daniel O’Donnell. So voted 5-0. Meeting adjourned at 6:08 
pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, Shawn M. Smith, Auditorium Commission Secretary

Recommendations
